L2.1 keystone: render-ui prop bound to a `@payload.X` / `@entity.X` / `@config.X` / SExpression operator whose resolved type doesn't match any of the prop's declared `types` in the patterns registry. Distinct from `RenderUIPropTypeMismatch` (literal-only); this rule uses the F3 binding resolver to walk through bindings and SExpression operator return types (sharpened by F2's `returnSemantics` for input-dependent operators). Gap #6 in `docs/Almadar_Std_Verification.md`.

L2.2: render-ui prop with `kind: "event-ref"` or `kind: "callback"` bound to an event-name string whose declared payload schema in the trait's `emits {}` block doesn't match the component's documented bus emit shape (registry's `emitPayloadSchema` for event-ref props; `callbackArgs` for callback props). Gap #32 in `docs/Almadar_Std_Verification.md`.

`notify` is sugar for `render-ui toast { type: alert, … }`, desugared at `.lolo` lowering (owner ruling 2026-09-11) — the `.orb` IR never carries a `notify` effect kind. A `notify` tuple reaching L2 means a hand-authored `.orb` or a registry not yet re-emitted.

Trait declares an event in its `emits[]` block but no transition fires it via `(emit X)` or operator emit-config success/failure. Usually a copy-paste leftover or a stale declaration after a rename; gap #2 defense in `docs/Almadar_Std_Verification.md`.
`orb validate --final`: a rendered control fires an event no trait handles — not the rendering trait, an embedder of it, nor a `listens` route (G-ORB-187).

Operator declares `requiresEmitSuccess: true` in canonical-operators.json but the effect call site is missing the trailing options object or its `emit.success` event key. Applies to fetch / persist / call-service by default; any future operator can opt in via the same JSON flag.
`deliver: ids` makes the success event's `data` a row-set reference; any use other than passing it whole as a `render-ui` prop value reads rows that were never delivered.
`total: none` skips the count, so the success event's `totalCount` is never set.

`(set @entity.X ?payloadField)` writes a payload field whose declared type does not match the target entity field's declared type. The lolo crate catches this at author time for `.lolo`; this is the raw-`.orb` defense-in-depth backstop. Payload field types are sourced from the trait's `emits[].payload_schema` and `listens` payload metadata.
A record literal written into an entity (a `persist` data literal, or a `set` into a relation field) names a key the entity does not declare.
A record literal written into an entity carries a value whose type the declared field does not admit.
A `persist create` data literal omits a column the entity requires (no default, not framework-stamped).

`(set @entity.X (op …))` assigns an operator/expression value whose inferred result type is incompatible with the target field's declared type (e.g. `(set @entity.count (str/concat …))` into a `number` field). The value's type is inferred *through* the S-expression via the canonical operator `return_semantics` lattice; an unknowable result (`Json`) never rejects (Gap G-LOLO-SET-OP-RETURN).

An ordering comparison (`<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`) whose operands infer to a number on one side and a string on the other. The JS runtime coerces, the compiled TypeScript does not typecheck, and Rust compares kinds — the paths disagree. Convert one side so both are the same kind.

An operator argument whose static type contradicts the type the operator table declares for its position — `(str/upper @entity.count)` with `count: number`, `(+ "a" 1)`. Both evaluators raise the same typed mismatch at run time (D-12), so the program can never do what it says.

A value handed to an operator has no determined type — an unresolved expression, an expression value, json, a loose union, a list whose items share no type — so it cannot be checked against the type the operator declares (or, at a type variable, what the variable stands for and the type of the result are unknown). Narrow it with `(as value T)` (checked, null on a misfit), or give it a real type (a declared payload or entity shape, a named union alias for a list of differently-shaped items).

An ordering comparison (`<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`) over an operand that can be missing or null — an optional entity field with no default, an optional payload field — that the program neither guards with a presence check (`(and (validate/required x) (< x 3))`, an `if`/`when` on presence) nor declares a default for. Both evaluators read a missing value as below any number; every push-down store fails the comparison, so the meaning is the program's to state.

An operand that can be missing or null — an optional entity field with no default, an optional payload field — handed to a position the kernel raises on when it is null (`rejectsNull` in the operator table), with no presence check or default in front of it. The program says what a missing value means: a guard, a default, or a required field.

`(set @entity.X @config.<knob>)` where the value is STILL the literal `@config.<knob>` token post-inline (no default resolved it, no call-site override supplied one) and `X` is a REQUIRED entity field. The emitter has nothing honest to assign — a required TS slot gets `undefined`. Give the knob a default or make the field optional.
`(emit EVT {...})` literal payload is missing a field the event's declared payload marks as required. Error severity.
`(emit EVT {...})` literal carries a field that is not declared on the event's payload schema. Error severity.
`(emit EVT {...})` literal provides a value whose primitive type does not match the declared `PayloadField.field_type`. Error severity.
An `emit` repeats an earlier one of the same transition identically: the dispatch loop collapses the second.

A render-ui pattern prop typed `EntityWith<K>` declares required entity fields (`requiredFields` in the registry), but the bound entity does not provide them and no remap/field-map supplies them. The component would render blank rows. Remap-aware (runs post-inline). Error severity.

**The payload invariant.** An event's declared payload type IS its access path: declaring `Survey` means the payload is the row (read `?name`); declaring `{ row : Survey }` means read `?row.name`. This fires when an event declares a field that the effect firing it does not actually emit — so every read of that field is `undefined` at runtime, even though `orb validate` and `orb verify` otherwise pass. Checked as width subtyping (`declared ⊆ produced`): declaring FEWER fields than are emitted is legal, declaring one that is never emitted is not. Replaces the narrower `EmitSuccessPayloadWrapped` (persist-only) and `EmitSuccessPayloadReturnMismatch` (empty-payload-only) checks. Error severity.
An effect (`emit`, `persist`, `set`, `notify`, …) inside the `fn` body of a collection operator: a lambda is evaluated for its value, an effect there never runs. Error severity.
Interactive component missing itemActions

The trait that OWNS a page's content region (`page_content_owner`'s `channel`/`sole-writer`) has a user-triggered arm that repaints its own main-slot body with something offering no way on: no content-body pattern, no registry event-kind prop bound to a live (non-lifecycle) event or an unresolved binding, and no `@trait.X` embed. "User- triggered" means the event is reachable from a rendered affordance or a `listens` route, transitively, minus async-result and lifecycle events. Exempt: an arm running its own `fetch`/`persist` (its result arm repaints); a non-self-transition escaping to a state with another producible, non-lifecycle arm. Ported from the JS wiring lint's `viewer-stranded`, predicate revised 2026-09-12 per the F31 live probe (`play_scene` on `ui-minigolf-board`/`std-chem-titration`): the JS's labelled-control test and `@`/`?` sigil branch were both heuristics and are dropped — a registry event-kind prop is the only test.
